text:
Bo Horvat does the hard minutes for the Islanders: he plays 21 a night and lately closer to 22, mostly against the other team's top line. Evolving-Hockey had his competition in the 99th percentile last season, which is the job description for an Islanders first-line center now that Matthew Schaefer is drawing everyone's eye from the back end.

He has 17 points in 17 games and 7 goals on 8.2 expected, so his scoring is close to honest, maybe a touch light. The Islanders get 54% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, five points better than without him. That's a center earning his ice time.

The recent stretch is quieter: 3 goals in ten games, with the Islanders winning only three of their last seven. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says 59% of his shots come off the rush, so his production rises and falls with how often the Islanders win the puck back in motion. Watch the transition game. When it's working, so is he.
headline: Horvat is better than his recent goals
